meta.title: China, in Fact — Wordmark Studies
meta.summary: Six black-and-white wordmark studies. These are selection proofs, not final outlined production logos.

preserve: Exact public name: China, in Fact
The comma remains part of the name
A usable wordmark before any standalone symbol

routes.label: 01 — The in inside China
routes.family: a second reading already hidden in the name
routes.rationale: The in inside China and the spoken in share one typographic voice. The idea is discovered after the name is read, not explained before it.
routes.prompt: Reveal the repeated in already present inside China while preserving the exact name and immediate readability.
routes.watch_out: The contrast must feel intentional, not like mixed-font decoration.
routes.decision_advice: The in inside China and the spoken in share one typographic voice. The idea is discovered after the name is read, not explained before it.

routes.label: 02 — Comma + i = 人
routes.family: English, punctuation, and a person in one reading
routes.rationale: The comma and the following i still read normally, while their two falling strokes quietly form 人 — person — for those who notice it.
routes.prompt: Let the comma and i form the two strokes of 人 without making Chinese knowledge necessary for reading the name.
routes.watch_out: Keep the hidden character quiet; the English reading comes first.
routes.decision_advice: The comma and the following i still read normally, while their two falling strokes quietly form 人 — person — for those who notice it.

routes.label: 03 — C holds 中
routes.family: a Latin entrance carrying a Chinese center
routes.rationale: The opening C contains 中, meaning middle or center. Without Chinese knowledge it remains a distinctive first letter; with it, a second layer appears.
routes.prompt: Build a readable initial C whose counter holds 中 as part of the same glyph, then keep the rest of the wordmark calm.
routes.watch_out: Do not let the combined glyph become a generic cultural badge.
routes.decision_advice: The opening C contains 中, meaning middle or center. Without Chinese knowledge it remains a distinctive first letter; with it, a second layer appears.

routes.label: 04 — A crowd becomes the comma
routes.family: many contributors making one shared pause
routes.rationale: The brand's indispensable comma is made from many unequal dots: individual presences that only together become the punctuation.
routes.prompt: Construct the comma from a small organic crowd while leaving the rest of the name typographically quiet.
routes.watch_out: The dots must merge into a comma at small sizes, not a digital halftone.
routes.decision_advice: The brand's indispensable comma is made from many unequal dots: individual presences that only together become the punctuation.

routes.label: 05 — The comma becomes Fact
routes.family: a pause that physically carries the reader onward
routes.rationale: The comma's tail travels through in and rises into the F of Fact. The punctuation performs the promise embedded in the name.
routes.prompt: Draw one continuous comma-to-F ligature that keeps China, in Fact readable in the correct order.
routes.watch_out: Avoid a decorative swoosh; every stroke must serve comma, reading order, or F.
routes.decision_advice: The comma's tail travels through in and rises into the F of Fact. The punctuation performs the promise embedded in the name.

routes.label: 06 — Found in China
routes.family: the explicit in is found beneath the in already inside China
routes.rationale: The two identical in pairs align vertically. The compact lockup makes the phrase feel discovered inside the name rather than attached as a slogan.
routes.prompt: Stack the wordmark so the two occurrences of in occupy one column and reveal the internal wordplay.
routes.watch_out: Retain the natural reading order and avoid poster-style hierarchy.
routes.decision_advice: The two identical in pairs align vertically. The compact lockup makes the phrase feel discovered inside the name rather than attached as a slogan.
